answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if it repeats a verified fraud pattern, while a rate limit lets each stake create only one trusted signal at a time. A sybil operator must therefore lock real capital across many accounts and risk losing it when those accounts coordinate abuse. The cost rises with the attack’s scale, unlike free account creation; a pearl-market agent might even wait on a terrace before granting trust, but the stake—not the setting—is the defense.
